advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the _write_event_file docstring in inbound_translate.py to note that finalize_event can now raise CommandError on a secret-screen refusal (not only best-effort signing).
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py:264: `signing failure is logged, never raised. repo_root is the tracker worktree's parent.`
src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:354: `screen_event(data)` then _seam.screen_event raises CommandError at :395 when a finding has no override reason
The new comment at inbound_translate.py:273-274 acknowledges 'A refusal raises CommandError', directly contradicting the older docstring two lines above it, which was not updated.
advisory.finding: The inline docstring for the reconciler's _write_event_file still asserts the write path is best-effort and never raises for content ('a signing failure is logged, never raised'), but after routing through _seam.finalize_event the call can now raise CommandError when a Jira comment/edit body matches a live credential shape — a new, un-noted failure mode for inbound translate.
advisory.suggested_fix: Amend the 'a signing failure is logged, never raised' sentence to add that the shared finalize seam additionally raises CommandError when a live-credential shape is detected, and that the caller's per-mutation backstop records-and-continues.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the workflow-file secret_scan intentionally drops the old broader length/entropy behavior, or restore lint-specific breadth so real embedded shorter-token credentials in workflow files are still flagged.
evidence: src/rebar/secret_screen.py:79: `("GitHub token", re.compile(r"\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}"), True)` — fixed length, entropy-checked
src/rebar/secret_screen.py:72: `_MIN_ENTROPY = 3.0` now applies to entropy-checked families in the lint sweep, which previously had no entropy floor at all
advisory.finding: lint.py's workflow-file secret_scan now consumes the shared SECRET_PATTERNS, which are tuned for LIVE store shapes (fixed full lengths + entropy floor) and are strictly NARROWER than the patterns it replaced (e.g. GitHub token was `gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}` now requires exactly `{36}`; Slack was `{10,}` now `{20}`; Stripe was `{16,}` now `{24}`; Slack webhook was `[A-Za-z0-9/]+` now `{40}`). Shorter or lower-entropy but still-embedded credential shapes in a workflow file that the old linter flagged will now pass silently.

The adjacent test_the_reconciler_and_importer_paths_are_screened_too exercises _seam.finalize_event directly, not inbound_translate._write_event_file, so the reconciler's own routing to the seam is verified only by the source grep.
advisory.finding: test_the_inbound_jira_translate_routes_through_the_shared_seam asserts on the SOURCE TEXT of inbound_translate.py ('_seam.finalize_event(' present, '_seam._apply_authorship(' absent) instead of exercising the reconciler write path, so it is a source-grepping change-detector that cannot detect a regression where the screen is present but non-functional, and breaks on any behavior-preserving refactor (aliasing/wrapping the seam call).
scenarios: A refactor renames finalize_event or introduces a passthrough wrapper — test breaks though behavior is unchanged.
The seam call is kept but the screen is disabled/bypassed downstream — source grep still passes, regression escapes.
advisory.suggested_fix: Call inbound_translate._write_event_file(tracker, ticket_id, "COMMENT", {"body": f"from jira: {_fake_secret('ghp_', 36)}"}) and assert pytest.raises(CommandError) plus that no *-COMMENT file was written under the ticket dir.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the MCP override-exclusion contract against the derived tool schema (parameter names of the registered @mcp.tool functions) rather than by grepping inspect.getsource for substrings.
evidence: source = inspect.getsource(module); assert "allow_secret_pattern" not in source

MCP tools are @mcp.tool-decorated functions (src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:150-153 'def comment_ticket(ticket_id: str, body: str)'), so their published schemas are derivable at runtime from the signatures rather than from source text.
advisory.finding: test_the_override_is_not_exposed_over_mcp asserts on inspect.getsource() substrings ('allow_secret_pattern'/'allow-secret-pattern' absent, and the exact literal 'rebar.comment(ticket_id, body)' present) — a source-grep of source under test that breaks on comments/docstrings/reformatting and does not verify the actual observable contract (the generated MCP tool schema lacks the parameter).
scenarios: comment_ticket call is reformatted to 'rebar.comment(ticket_id, body,)' or wrapped — exact-literal assertion fails though the schema is unchanged.
A docstring or comment in _mcp_writes mentions 'allow_secret_pattern' — the absence assertion fails spuriously.
advisory.suggested_fix: Register the MCP write tools and assert that no tool's input schema contains an 'allow_secret_pattern' property, instead of substring-scanning the module source.
